title: add transactional downgrade-guard, backup/restore and version-pinning to private-installer upgrade tooling
author: Ava Martinez
description: Motivation: Private deployments need safe, auditable upgrade and rollback semantics for production databases and installer state. This PR introduces an upgrade/rollback tooling surface in the private-installer that implements: 1) version pinning for component charts and terraform modules to avoid unintended implicit upgrades, 2) an automated pre-upgrade backup and post-upgrade validation flow for Postgres and object storage snapshots, 3) transactional schema migrations (migrate up/down) with a downgrade guard that blocks incompatible downgrades, and 4) CLI hooks and Helm/Terraform module updates to expose rollback primitives to operators. The change is intended to reduce upgrade risk in customer air-gapped and VPC deployments and to provide clear operator-runbooks for emergency rollbacks. Checklist: - [x] Add version pinning config and validation on install/upgrade - [x] Implement backup hook that captures Postgres logical dump + S3-compatible object store snapshot - [x] Implement restore hook and verification steps - [x] Add transactional migration runner (uses transactional DDL pattern where supported) - [x] Add downgrade-guard check that compares current schema version and checks migration reversibility before permitting a downgrade - [x] Update Helm charts, Terraform module variables, and installer CLI flags - [x] Add e2e installer test harness integration and unit tests - [x] Update docs and operator runbook (private-installer/README-UPGRADES.md). This description includes links and runbook references: see internal doc https://linear.redwood.ai/ENG-2345 and SUP ticket SUP-1123. The description is intentionally concise; see commits and review thread for details.

review_thread: Riley Chen: Nice work. Two questions: 1) Do we have a strategy for large DBs where logical dump is impractical?  Suggest we add a streaming snapshot fallback. 2) The downgrade-guard should be pluggable so customers can opt-out for controlled test environments.

Ava Martinez: Reply: Added S3 snapshot adapter and streaming fallback in installer/hooks/backup.sh. The downgrade-guard is opt-out via --allow-unsafe-downgrade flag in the CLI but default remains conservative. See commit 'add streaming-snapshot-fallback'

Nikhil Rao: Security review: ensure backups are encrypted and KMS-integrated by default for private deployments. Also add RBAC for restore operations so only operators with the restore role can run restore hooks.
Ava Martinez: Reply: Added KMS integration in terraform module variables and enforce role binding in installer. Tests cover KMS path.

merge_outcome: merged via squash, commit message: 'Add transactional downgrade-guard, backup/restore and version-pinning to private-installer (ENG-2345)'. Merged after two approvals and green CI. Cherry-picked small revert to address transient e2e timeout; final CI green before merge.
release_notes: Private-installer: Added safe upgrade/rollback tooling: version pinning, pre-upgrade backup and post-upgrade verification, transactional migrations and downgrade guard. Operators should review private-installer/README-UPGRADES.md for runbook and required IAM/KMS settings.
notes: Backed out a flakey helper in migrations/runner.go on 2026-02-16, reworked streaming snapshot to be incremental for large DBs. Operator runbook added and linked. This PR touches both Helm and Terraform modules; coordinate with infra team for terraform registry version bump.
validation_steps: 1) Run installer --dry-run against staging cluster; 2) Trigger upgrade with --enable-backup and verify backup artifacts are created in S3-compatible bucket; 3) Validate migration runner applies and records schema_version; 4) Attempt a downgrade without --allow-unsafe-downgrade and confirm guard blocks action; 5) Test restore flow and verify service health checks pass.
